label: prop:genus-maximal-descent
title: Genus of the one-complex-dimensional descent
html:
Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe satisfying the Descartes condition \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 (Descartes condition). If the geometric descent produces a compact one-complex-dimensional base M_0, then M_0 is a Riemann surface of genus g = 4.

More precisely: if the categorical Euler characteristic \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) = -6 equals the topological Euler characteristic \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) of the base curve, then Gauss--Bonnet on M_0 gives 2(1 - g) = -6, hence g = 4. That identification is a hypothesis here, not a consequence: taking \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 and 2(1 - g) = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) as inputs determines g = 4 and the automorphism bound below. The Hurwitz bound |\mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma)| \leq 84(g - 1) then gives |\mathrm{Aut}(M_0)| \leq 252. The bound holds for every genus g \geq 2, so it does not single out g = 4; the genus is fixed by the Euler characteristic alone. Bring's curve, the genus-4 curve used later, has automorphism group S_5 of order 120, below the bound.
